title: Mini brain organoids ‘reading’ Braille marks key step towards biohybrid computing
script:
Bristol researchers just ran Braille through living brain tissue.
Your next computer processor might be partially biological.
Tianyi Liu and Benjamin Ward-Cherrier at the University of Bristol merged brain organoids with silicon.
They used a multi-electrode array to pulse Braille patterns into the tissue.
Three organoids working together decoded the data with eighty-three percent accuracy.
The team used human stem cells to grow these mini-brains for biohybrid tests.
This setup mimics the massive energy efficiency of human neural pathways.
Next, the Bristol team will test if these biological systems can learn. Would you use a PC powered by living cells?
